articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about your first visit to the SSV Normandy SR-2, including where to find all collectibles and pick the right dialogue choices for your playthrough.

Looking for something specific? Click the links below to jump to...

After boarding the Normandy, you'll be in a dream sequence, where you must chase after the small child in the distance. He will run away a few times, and eventually the dream will end when Shepard catches up with him.

Shepard will then awaken, and will soon find Liara tapping on their door. After discussing the dream (or turtling up about it), you'll be interrupted by Specialist Samantha Traynor, who introduces herself and gives you a very quick overview of the important floors and rooms of the Normandy. For those who have played Mass Effect 2, the most important changes are as follows:

The Tech Lab, Armory and Briefing Room in the rear of the CIC deck have been removed. In their place is a new Vid Comm and the War Room, which require passing through a security scanner first.

Miranda's old XO office has been taken over by Liara, and Kasumi's area is now a recreation lounge.

The Cargo Bay, previously only visited at the end of Mass Effect 2, can now be accessed at any time, and is where the Armory functions have been moved to.

Shepard will then go to the Vid Comm and talk with Admiral Hackett again. You can get Morality Points in this conversation:

When Shepard relays what happened with the Council... Pick "I understand their concerns" for +2 Paragon Points . Pick "They're useless" for +2 Renegade Points .

Pick "I understand their concerns" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "They're useless" for +2 Renegade Points .

After Hackett talks about you helping to defend the Prothean device... Pick "And Earth?" for +2 Paragon Points . "We'll get it done" for +2 Renegade Points .

Pick "And Earth?" for +2 Paragon Points .

"We'll get it done" for +2 Renegade Points .

After this, you'll regain full control of Shepard, and at last be able to explore the Normandy at your leisure!

You'll begin in the Vid Comm room of the CIC Deck. The CIC, or Combat Information Center, is the business deck of the ship. The Vid Comm usually doesn't offer much on its own, but Shepard will make important calls to various leaders of the galaxy in this room. Optional Vid Comm calls are rare, but Specialist Traynor will let you know when you can make a call.

The War Room is the cramped circular room just outside the Vid Comm room. This is where Shepard makes plans for the war, as well as where important military guests will station themselves. The most important part of the War Room is the War Terminal, which allows Shepard to review their War Assets and other Galaxy at War stats.

Galaxy at War is a very important mechanic in Mass Effect 3 because it directly ties into how well Shepard's efforts will be during the Reaper War, but it can be a bit confusing to figure out. Here's how it works:

War Assets - These are the groups, ships, technologies and individuals that you've recruited for your cause. These are given a numerical value known a "Total Military Strength".

Total Military Strength (TMS) - This is the rating for how strong each individual War Asset can be. The TMS of a War Asset can be increased or decreased by your actions. For example, the TMS of the Normandy will be increased if you bought any of the three important upgrades for it in Mass Effect 2. In this guide, we refer to the value of your War Assets using TMS, since that's a locked value unaffected by your Galactic Readiness.

In this guide, we refer to the value of your War Assets using TMS, since that's a locked value unaffected by your Galactic Readiness.

Galactic Readiness - This refers to how ready your War Assets are to assist you when you need them, and can be affected by playing Mass Effect: Datapad, the N7 HQ website (both now defunct), or the Multiplayer mode. The lowest it can get is 50%. SEE BELOW FOR AN IMPORTANT NOTE ON THIS.

Effective Military Strength (EMS) - This final step is when your TMS and Galactic Readiness are combined into a final rating, where the Galactic Readiness percentage cuts into your TMS. For example, if your TMS is 800 and your Galactic Readiness is 50%, then your Effective Military Strength will be 400.

This sounds like a LOT, and it is, but to sum it up, you increase your chances of a positive outcome to the war by collecting and bolstering War Assets via Story Missions and Side Missions . Ignoring Side Missions in particular will vastly decrease your chances, especially in the Legendary Edition.

At the start of the game, Shepard hasn't made any alliances yet and so only has Alliance forces to work with. Your past actions may have already earned you a few bonuses however, including surplus Mineral Resources from Mass Effect 2. Many War Assets you earn later in the game will also be influenced by your past actions. Everything's important!

Outside of the War Room is the old Briefing Room table, now in a makeshift room in the side of the exit hallway. This can't be interacted with, and will only be used when the story requires it.

Alliance Shuttle - On the crates in the corner of the hallway, to the right of the Briefing Room.

This is the earliest point in time you can find a Model Ship. These are the ships that Shepard bought back in Mass Effect 2, but most are available for all players. These are also covered in a dedicated page:

Out in the main CIC area you'll find Samantha Traynor at her post on the corner of the Galaxy Map. While she was only brought on to help with the retrofit, the hasty escape from Earth has meant that she's had to reassign herself as your Specialist.

Traynor will let you know when you have new messages at your Private Terminal, when you've unlocked a new N7 Mission or one of her own discoveries, or when someone wants to speak with you at the Vid Comm. Traynor is also the earliest Romance option, who is only interested in a Female Shepard.

Approaching Traynor will also add the " N7: Cerberus Lab " Side Mission to your Journal. Nice!

The Private Terminal is located on the opposite corner of the Galaxy Map from Traynor. You can do a couple of things here (depending on your version):

Email - All of your messages. Rather than being manually sorted into "Unread" and "Archived", in Mass Effect 3 they'll simply grey out. Emails will always be listed in the order you received them.

Advanced Combat Training - Three video tutorials that cover Squad Commands, using Powers, and Real-Time Control (using both at once without pausing the game). This option is removed in the Legendary Edition.

Squad Selection - In Mass Effect 3, this is now only available via the Private Terminal in the Captain's Cabin. This lets you review the full Abilities and Powers list of each Squad Mate, as well as the weapons you've equipped for them, and their passive Armor Bonus that they grant when you pick them for your Squad.

If you have the From Ashes DLC, reading "Priority Mission: Eden Prime" will add the similarly-named " Priority: Eden Prime " mission to your Journal.

The Bridge is the cockpit area at the very front of the ship, and is where you can talk to your pilot, Joker. Talk to him and you'll have a brief chat about how things went with the Council.

That's everything on the CIC, so head to the elevator behind the Galaxy Map and go down to the Crew's Quarters.

The Crew's Quarters, otherwise known as the Crew Deck is unique because it's the only deck of the ship that you exit backwards out of the elevator, meaning you'll be facing the opposite direction compared to the other three decks. The area behind the elevator is the Mess Hall, which is where the crew will make meals and generally hang out.

The rear of the Crew Deck out of the elevator is different from Mass Effect 2 because it has no specific person here, at least not yet. More frequently, these rooms will be where various characters will chill out: if somebody isn't in their usual spot, it's likely that they're either here, in the Mess Hall, or at another character's post. The only room that'll be locked is the bathroom of the opposite gender to Shepard's: you can't barge into it like you could in Mass Effect 2.

Destiny Ascension - Located in the back corner of the Life Support room, near the white table with the coffee mug on it.

Liara's Cabin is located on the Port side of the ship, via the door behind the kitchen area in the mess hall. Head inside and you'll meet Glyph, Liara's Broker VI Drone (who you may have met before in the previous game!). It'll introduce you to the Intel terminal, which you can use to research intel that lets you choose one of two minor buffs.

If you completed Lair of the Shadow Broker in Mass Effect 2, you'll have one already, which lets you upgrade either your Shield Strength or Ammo Capacity by 5%. If you're playing New Game Plus and were able to carry the Prejek Paddlefish from Mass Effect 2 all the way through, you can also choose to increase either your Weapon or Power Damage by 10%.

Now you'll want to talk to Liara and have a proper catch-up with her. If you Romanced her in Mass Effect 1, then she'll directly ask if you want to continue the relationship:

Pick "Absolutely" to resume the relationship. If you had previously rekindled a Romance with Liara in Mass Effect 2's Lair of the Shadow Broker DLC , this will Lock In your Romance with her again for Mass Effect 3, which locks you out of all other Romances.

If you had previously rekindled a Romance with Liara in Mass Effect 2's Lair of the Shadow Broker DLC , this will Lock In your Romance with her again for Mass Effect 3, which locks you out of all other Romances.

Pick "Let's just be friends" to cease the Romance for good, giving you the option to Romance somebody else later.

Whether you go through this or not, you'll get +2 Reputation for talking with her.

Once the conversation is over, make sure to talk to Liara a second time to learn more about what she's been up to in the past six months. You can also use the Broker Terminal to read some messages that Liara has given you access to. These don't give any rewards.

On the opposite side of the Mess Hall from Liara's Cabin will be the Medical Lab, the room with the windows. Here you can catch up with the doctor you recruited back in Huerta Memorial Hospital, who'll request a medical check-up.

She'll explain that Shepard's facial scars from Mass Effect 2 can return if you make Renegade choices, but will stay away if you make Paragon ones ...although if you used the Med-Bay Upgrade to permanently heal them in Mass Effect 2, this is carried over to 3 and thus is a non-issue.

If you didn't use Mass Effect 2's Med-Bay Upgrade but prefer to have an un-scarred face while making Renegade Choices, you'll be able to heal them by using some Intel obtained from the " Citadel: Medical Supplies " Side Mission.

Also in back-right corner of the Medical Bay are two objects over the empty bed, which you can use to adjust the Powers for Shepard and their squad:

Reassign Powers - You can reset your Ability Points to redistribute them across your Powers (or your Squad Mates) with this device. The first use will be free, while additional ones will cost Credits .

Reassign Power Bonuses - By conversing with your Squad Members you can gain the ability to learn one of their Powers, which you can then learn to use yourself here as a Bonus Power. You haven't unlocked any yet, but keep talking with your Squad and progressing their personal storylines and you'll unlock them as you go. Unlike Mass Effect 2, in Mass Effect 3 your Squad will unlock several!

The door in the back of the Medical Center leads to the AI Core, although nothing's in there for now except for the body of Dr. Eva Coré after you recovered it from Mars.

Engineering is the second-smallest deck on the Normandy SR-2, so exploring it won't take long. First, you may notice that the door on the far left at the end of the corridor, labeled Port Cargo, is locked. You'll need to complete the " From Ashes " DLC Mission to open this, which was available as a pre-order bonus in the original release of Mass Effect 3 and then later as DLC (it's included in the Wii U and Legendary Editions).

For now, head through one of the doors next to the elevator. Unfortunately Gabby and Ken aren't there, but you will find an old friend from Mass Effect 1: Engineer Adams! As with the first game, he's more than happy to explain the workings of the Normandy, especially how the SR-2 compares to the original SR-1. You'll get +2 Reputation just for talking with him.

You may have noticed some red-lit stairs as you made your way to Engineer Adams. These lead to the Engineering Subdeck in the guts of the ship, although it's unoccupied these days. Here you'll be able to find several different collectibles:

That's all there is to do down here, so it's time to go to the final area of Engineering.

In the Starboard Cargo deck (the door to the far right of the elevator) will be where Diana Allers has set herself up, forming a makeshift studio aboard the Normandy. Talk to her and she'll express interest in the fact that the Normandy has direct communication with Earth, letting you pick the tone for her support.

Pick "Get us support" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "Focus on Cerberus" for +2 Renegade Points .

You'll also get +2 Reputation for talking with her.

You can also kick Allers off the ship if you want by talking to her twice in a row. Do note that this will eliminate the chance for Reputation, Morality Points and EMS via several interviews after major story events.

The Shuttle Bay was previously only visited just once at the end of Mass Effect 2. However the Armory has been moved down here, so you can now visit it at any time! You'll first want to talk to Steve Cortez, who's manning a station just to your right. Right off the bat, you can get some Morality Points:

Pick "At ease there, soldier" for +2 Paragon Points .

Pick "What's the situation?" for +2 Renegade Points .

Unlike the Kodiak from Mass Effect 2, Cortez is the face of your shuttle, taking you to any Missions you'll be undertaking. Like Traynor he's also a Romance option, and is only interested in Male Shepards. As always, make sure to talk to Cortex a few more times to hear more from him.

Surrounding Cortez's posts will be four terminals that all relate to Shepard's Weapons and Equipment. We'll cover them from left to right.

On the far left is the Weapon Bench, like the one you found on Mars. With this, you can change Shepard's Weapon loadout and what mods are applied to each and every one of their Weapons. Each weapon can only hold two Mods at once, and several are mutually exclusive: you cannot apply both an Extended Barrel and a High-Velocity Barrel at the same time, for example. Changing the loadouts of Squad Mates can only be done immediately before a Mission.

In the middle-left is the Weapon Upgrade terminal. Here you can spend Credits to upgrade a Weapon, which will improve its weight, ammo capacity, damage and accuracy. Every Weapon can be upgraded through to Level V (5) on a first run, and then to Level X (10) in New Game Plus. Picking up a Weapon a second time in New Game Plus will automatically upgrade it by three levels, leaving you to manually upgrade it to Level VIII, IX and X via this terminal.

In the middle-right will be the Procurement Interface. As Cortez explained, the Procurement Interface allows you to buy items available from any store on the Citadel that you've visited at least once. The downside is that there's a 10% markup for having the item delivered to the Normandy, since, y'know, there's a war on.

The Procurement Interface does have one very handy use however, and that is checking to see updated stock. It's a huge time sink to go to the Citadel and then manually visit each and every store kiosk there, but the Procurement Interface lets you check all their stock in a single menu right from the Normandy!

On the far-right side is the Armor Locker, which lets you change and customize Shepard's armor. Each armor piece will give a minor buff, but you can also elect to use full custom suits with a more bespoke look (although these cannot be visually customized). You can also change Shepard's casual clothes, which are what they wear while on board the Normandy and on the Citadel.

You can talk to James in his little bodybuilding nook on the left side of the Cargo Bay. Here you'll get into a fisticuff sparring match with him, where you learn about his backstory (as told in the Paragon Lost movie) and use Paragon or Renegade Interrupts during the fight. They're easy to miss, so be sure to react fast!

You'll get no Morality Points for the Interrupts, but you will get +5 Reputation and unlock James' Fortification as a Bonus Power. Remember to talk to James after the sparring matching to learn more about him, and poke him a few more times after that to hear a few comments.

If you have the Collector's, Deluxe or Legendary Edition of the game, you may have noticed a white robot dog walking around with a blue scanner. This is KEI-9, and the scanner means it's looking for Shepard. The scanner can be rather distracting during conversations, but you can turn it off for your visit by walking up to and interacting with KEI-9 whenever you visit here.

The Cargo Bay has a wide assortment of Ship Models to find, so we've broken it out into its own section.

The final area of the ship is the Captain's Cabin at the top, which is a mostly cosmetic area. Any fish you acquire on the Citadel will be displayed here on the left, however the catch is that you must feed them after every Mission or else they'll die. While this is easier on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S (faster loading times and all that), you'll be able to buy an Aquarium VI for 25,000 Credits that will do that for you.

The office across from the fish tank has its own Private Terminal. It works just like the one next to the Galaxy map on the CIC, except this one still lets you review your Squad and change their appearances. Sadly, the photo of your previous Romance partner is not visible, and you can no longer view the medal to see your Trophies / Achievements.

Here will also be a glass wall with a collection of all the Ship Models you've found thus far. The Normandy SR-2 model is there by default, while the rest are found throughout the Normandy. Now however a second wall has been added for the extra ship models exclusive to Mass Effect 3, as well as the Shadow Broker Ship Model if you picked that up in the Mass Effect 2 DLC. This area is purely cosmetic, but everyone loves miniatures, right?

In the lower area of the cabin is the Armor Locker, which works just like the one in the Cargo Bay. You should know how it works by now!

The final thing we'd like to point out is the Sound System clock, which plays through a variety of music tracks. Unlike Mass Effect 2's Sound Systems, this can only be turned on or off, and will automatically move on to a random track when the current one ends. As well, it has its own unique music rather than using those from the soundtracks of a previous game. Here's your tracklist selection:

Reintegration Time - Shout Out Out Out Out

The Logistic Nightmare - Normals Welcome

articles.summary: Many fun quests exist in Hello Kitty Island Adventure, but none more exciting than celebrating the Birthday of your friends. Birthday Quests are a great way to
articles.body:
Many fun quests exist in Hello Kitty Island Adventure , but none more exciting than celebrating the Birthday of your friends. Birthday Quests are a great way to spend time with your favorite characters and learn more about them while exploring Friendship Island. In this guide, we’ll teach you all there is to know about these limited-time events, what’s to be gained from it, and all of the Birthdays recorded in Hello Kitty Island Adventure so far.

Birthday Quests are short events that will pop up a few days before the actual character’s birthday listed below. Like any other quest, they involve handling some errands for island residents to help them set up preparations, handle some discourse, or simply celebrate the day of their birth however they’d prefer. If you’re afraid of missing the day, don’t be! Birthday Quests extend outside of the character's birthday and will alert the player with a new quest in their menu, so there’s a good window for you to catch the quest before it’s gone for the year.

While completing the birthday quests won’t result in Friendship points like other quests will, it can still reward you with some exclusive items that you can’t get at any other time of the year. Once the quest is complete and you’ve celebrated the birthday with a selfie of the cast, you’ll be given a Party Favor and Birthday Balloons Crafting Plans . You can display these items just like any other furniture in your cabins to remember the wonderful day you spent with the birthday character.

To prepare for the year, here are all of the birthdays that have been recorded in Hello Kitty Island Adventure. Mark the dates and don't be late.

articles.title: Upcoming New Video Game Movies and TV Shows: 2026 Release Dates and Beyond
articles.summary: From The Legend of Zelda movie to The Last of Us, Fallout and Mass Effect TV shows -- and beyond -- here's every video game adaptation that's coming to the big and small screen!
articles.body:
Some may say we are in a renaissance of video game adaptations as we've been treated to The Super Mario Bros. Movie (and its sequel!), a third Sonic the Hedgehog film, and TV series based on The Last of Us and Fallout, and will soon be getting adaptations of God of War, Mass Effect, and so many more. The best part? A lot of these look so much better than video game adaptations we’ve gotten in the past.

How many will actually make it through development and see the light of day remains to be seen, and only a fraction of these have actual release dates. But we're watching these projects, and we're tracking them!

For the purposes of this list, we classify a “video game movie” or "video game TV show" as an actual adaptation of an existing video game, so something like Wreck-It Ralph (which is just a movie about video games) wouldn’t qualify. They don’t have to be faithful adaptations – they just have to be based on a real game.

Click on through the slideshow below for a glimpse, or read on to find out about the biggest projects with definite details. And if you see something incorrect, missing, or in need of an update, let us know in the comments!

What Are the Next Video Game Movies and TV Shows Coming Out? 2026 and Beyond Release Dates

The Angry Birds Movie 3 (January 29, 2027)

A Minecraft Movie Squared (July 23, 2027)

Tomb Raider Series (Sophie Turner) (TBA)

Splinter Cell: Deathwatch Season 2 (TBA)

Jason Sudeikis, Josh Gad, Rachel Bloom, and Danny McBride return as Red, Chuck, Silver, and Bomb for a third Angry Birds movies. John Rice (The Angry Birds Movie 1, Beavis & Butt-Head Do the Universe) directs from a screenplay by Thurop Van Orman (The Angry Birds Movie 2!).

The Sonic movies are going strong (Sonic 3 is at the top of our best video game movies of all time list!), so it's no surprise that a fourth film is in the works. There aren't many details available about the project yet, but based on the Sonic 3 post-credits scene , expect Amy Rose and Metal Sonic to show up.

The Legend of Zelda is officially getting the live-action film treatment and it's being produced by Nintendo's Shigeru Miyamoto and Avi Arad, chairman of Arad Productions and former founder and CEO of Marvel Studios.

The film will be directed by Wes Ball and will star Bo Bragason as Zelda and Benjamin Evan Ainsworth as Link. and it's all being co-financed by Nintendo and Sony Pictures Entertainment Inc. Nintendo will be financing more than 50% of the movie and the theatrical distribution will be done by Sony.

"The Legend of Zelda follows Link, a young warrior destined to protect the magical kingdom of Hyrule from the forces of darkness," the official description reads. "The land is under threat from Ganon, a ruthless warlord who seeks the Triforce — an ancient relic said to grant limitless power. To stop him, Link must embark on a perilous journey, battling monstrous creatures, exploring treacherous dungeons, and solving intricate puzzles to uncover sacred artifacts that can aid him in his quest."

If, like us, you can't wait for The Legend of Zelda movie, be sure to check out that one time we predicted the film would eventually arrive via an April Fools' Day joke.

Warner Bros. has officially confirmed A Minecraft Movie 2 will be released on July 23, 2027, and it makes sense as the original made over $957 million at the global box office. Will Jennifer Coolidge be back with her nitwit villager love interest? We can only hope!

At CES 2025, Sony announced that the wildly successful Helldivers 2 would be adapted into a major motion picture from Sony Productions and Sony Pictures. Director Justin Lin said the following at CinemaCon 2026: "Helldivers balances satire with humanity... and the only person who I think can pull this off is Jason Momoa." Momoa will be playing a soldier battling aliens on behalf of humanity.

A live-action Elden Ring movie is in the works from Ex Machina's Alex Garland, who will be directing and writing the movie for A24. George R.R. Martin is onboard as a producer. For those worried, Garland put together a 160-page draft script with 40 extra pages of images to convince Bandai Namco and FromSoftware to let him lead this project.

Activision and Paramount Pictures have announced that Yellowstone creator Tyler Sheridan and Lone Survivor's Peter Berg are onboard to lead the upcoming Call of Duty movie. Sheridan will write and produce and Berg will write, direct, and produce.

In Mortal Kombat 2, Karl Urban joined the series as Johnny Cage while Adeline Rudolph took on the role of Kitana. We gave the movie an 8/10 , saying "The bar for video game movie sequels isn’t very high, but this one not only clears the bar, it twirls it around like a bo staff." No word yet on if Mortal Kombat 3 is definitely happening, but we're pretty sure it will -- and if it does, hopefully it will answer our biggest burning questions about Mortal Kombat 2 .

Sony Pictures has an R-rated animated film based on Bloodborne in the works, though no details beyond the fact that it's being produced by YouTuber Jacksepticeye have been revealed yet.

Now that the second movie, The Super Mario Galaxy Movie, has hit theaters, fans are just waiting for word on what's next. Super Smash Bros. Movie maybe...?

A third movie in the popular series is said to be in development at Blumhouse Productions.

Even before Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 was out, it was confirmed the game would be getting a film adaptation. Developer Sandfall Interactive has partnered with Story Kitchen to bring this to life, but we don't know much else at this point.

Horizon Zero Dawn has had both a movie and a TV show in the works, but the TV show has had a bit of a rocky road. In July 2024, it was reported that the series was no longer moving forward at Netflix. It may show up again in the future, but it wasn't a great sign.

As for the movie, Sony announced at CES 2025 that a big-screen adaptation of Aloy's adventure is currently very early in production. A recent report said the movie is planning on filming in 2026 and releasing at some point in 2027.

In 2025, it was reported that this popular Roblox game would be getting a movie. We'll see if this one ever happens, but stranger adaptations of games have become a reality before!

EA's long-running life simulation series The Sims is getting the big-screen treatment from Loki season 1 director Kate Heron and Margot Robbie's production company Lucky Chap. We have yet to learn anything else about the project, but it should be welcome news for fans nonetheless.

Ubisoft's extreme sports game Riders Republic is getting a film adaptation from Bad Boys for Life's Adil El Arbi and Bilall Fallah. Ubisoft said it is "poised to be an electrifying action movie, delivering non-stop thrills, humor, and spectacular stunts on the snowy slopes of the Alps."

Netflix has partnered with The Coalition to develop a Gears of War live-action movie and an adult animated series. The movie will arrive first and, if these projects do well, there is “potential for more stories to follow!”

In March 2023, it was announced that the Gears of War movie will be written by Dune and Doctor Strange's Jon Spaihts. John Wick director David Leitch is in the helmer's chair when and if the project happens.

MCU star Simu Liu got fans excited when he said he was working with the rights holders to bring Sleeping Dogs to the big screen, and it turns out he is actually set to produce the film and play the lead role of Wei Shen. Timo Tjahjanto. Tjahjanto (The Beekeeper 2, Nobody 2) will direct.

In June, 2025, it was reported that Blumhouse Productions and James Wan's Atomic Monster would be adapting the first-person puzzle game Phasmophobia into a film. No word on the project since then, however.

Hideo Kojima's Kojima Productions has partnered with A24 to adapt Death Stranding into a live-action feature film.

"The film promises to delve into the mysteries surrounding the apocalyptic event called the 'Death Stranding', which blurred the lines between life and death, and brought forth nightmarish creatures into a world on the brink of collapse," the official synopsis reads. It was also confirmed it will "tell a story you haven't seen in that world."

A new animated film called Death Stranding: Mosquito is also on its way and, according to Kojima and animation director Hiroshi Miyamoto, it follows the story of "a guy who sucks." We got a look at a snippet of animation from the film at the Beyond the Strand presentation, which showed a man "with something stuck to his face that has a weird tentacle thing coming out of it. He's in the water at the beginning of the clip, swimming and approaching something human-shaped that's difficult to make out. But in the second part of the clip, he's on land, in the Timefall, fighting a guy in a porter suit, still with the gooey thing on his face." OK then!

There's always a lighthouse, and apparently there's always a BioShock adaptation in the works. After a previous attempt to bring the beloved first-person shooter to film form fell apart at Universal years ago, Netflix and Take-Two announced in early 2022 that a BioShock film adaptation is in the works for the streaming service. Hunger Games director Francis Lawrence is on-board to direct the film and Logan and Blade Runner 2049 writer Michael Green will pen the script for the story that will be “really true to the game itself.”

In October 2023, it was confirmed the was still in the writing stage but that the team was very optimistic about how the project was going, and in July 2024 producer Roy Lee said the film was still in the works but with a reduced budget.

Strange Scaffold's third-person neo-noir shooter, El Paso, Elsewhere, is getting the big screen treatment, and LaKeith Stanfield is said to be in talks to star and produce the project alongside Lorenzo di Bonaventura's Di Bonaventura Pictures and Colin Stark. The film would follow protagonist James Savage as he navigates a monster-filled world and tries to stop his vicious ex-girlfriend and the demons he is battling inside.

In 2025, Story Kitchen was in the process of gathering a team together to work on an adaptation of Hazelight Studios' Split Fiction. Reports say Sydney Sweeney may star in the film, Wicked director Jon M. Chu will direct, and Deadpool and Wolverine's screenwriter Rhett Reese and Paul Wernick are also on board.

Michael B. Jordan and Christopher McQuarrie are reportedly attached to a feature film adaptation of Electronic Arts’ bestselling military video game Battlefield. McQuarrie will write, direct and produce. Jordan is attached to produce and possibly star. EA will also serve as a producer on the Battlefield movie. The package is currently being shopped to studios, including Sony and Apple. The movie is meant to be a theatrical not streaming release.

Netflix’s The Witcher returned for its fourth season, and it did so with a new Geralt of Rivia as The Hunger Games’ Liam Hemsworth replaced Henry Cavill. You can watch all of those episodes now while knowing a fifth and final season is also in the works.

After a stellar first and second season, HBO's The Last of Us will be returning for a third season on HBO and it looks to, as the games did, switch the focus to Kaitlyn Dever's Abby for a while. Co-creator Craig Mazin confirmed this new season will be longer than Season 2.

While you wait, be sure to check out our explainer of the ending of Season 2 and how it sets up this next part of the tragic tale of The Last of Us.

A Ghost of Tsushima anime is on the way from Sony and Aniplex and it is set to launch exclusively on Crunchyroll in 2027. Instead of adapting the main game, this anime will instead focus on the Legends co-op multiplayer portion that was added post-launch.

Prime Video has officially announced that a God of War live-action series is in the works from Sony Pictures Television and PlayStation Productions. The show will follow the story that began in 2018’s God of War and will see Kratos and Atreus traveling to the highest peak in the nine realms of Norse mythology to spread the ashes of their late wife/mother.

At CES 2024, Sony confirmed writing was underway for the series. In October 2024, it was reported that Ronald D. Moore (Star Trek: The Next Generation, Battlestar Galactica, Outlander) had replaced the show's previous producers Rafe Judkins, Hawk Ostby and Mark Fergus as showrunner.

Season 2 of Prime Video's Fallout series switched to a weekly schedule (after Season 1's binge model), which certainly made it more "sticky" in the pop-culture conversation. And a Season 3 is in the works, though we don't know when it will hit. We do know, however, that Ella Purnell's Lucy and Walton Goggins' Ghoul will certainly be back.

Phoebe Waller-Bridge's live-action Tomb Raider series for Amazon Prime Video is back after appearing to be dead, and it will in fact star Sophie Turner as the legendary Lara Croft. Production will begin in January 2026 and Chad Hodge has signed on as co-showrunner alongside Jonathan van Tulleken as director and executive producer.

Netflix's Castlevania showrunner Adi Shankar released a new anime series based on Devil May Cry in April, 2025. Season 2 was released in May, 2026, and we gave it an 8/10 . The following month, Netflix confirmed that a third and final season was in the works.

Noah Hawley (Alien: Earth, Fargo, Legion) will be turning Far Cry into a TV series for FX and Hulu, along with It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia's Rob Mac (aka Rob McElhenney). Mac will also star in the series, which is in early days at the moment but is sure to be a major push for FX considering how much attention Alien: Earth received. Each season of the show will focus on a new setting, similar to the games.

A Mass Effect movie adaptation was in the works at least as far back as 2010, though it never wound up happening.

In December, 2021, however, it was reported that Amazon was working on a deal to adapt the game as a TV series. It once again took a while, but in November 2024, it was confirmed that Amazon MGM studios had begun development on the TV version . Daniel Casey (10 Cloverfield Lane) will write and executive produce the show, while other producers include EA/BioWare's Michael Gamble, who's leading development on the next Mass Effect game, and Avi Arad, who was part of that initial movie announcement all those years back.

PlayStation and Quantic Dream’s Beyond: Two Souls could be getting a TV series from original star Elliot Page. Reports indicate that Page’s Pageboy Productions has acquired the rights tor the project, which is said to be in early development.

Netflix is producing a live-action Assassin's Creed series, executive produced by Ubisoft's Jason Altman and Danielle Kreinik. The live-action series will be an "epic, genre-bending live action adaptation." The collaboration will "tap into the iconic video game’s trove of dynamic stories" to create live-action, animated and anime series. The series will be set in Ancient Rome, starting in the year 64 AD.

Back in 2012, it was reported that Tom Hardy was going to be starring as Sam Fisher in a film adaptation of Splinter Cell, but that obviously never panned out. Instead, the Netflix series Splinter Cell: Deathwatch released a first season in 2025, with Liev Schreiber voicing Fisher. A second season is in the works.

A24 and Netflix will be bringing us a reality TV show based on the chaotic cooking game known as Overcooked. It is said to be an unscripted format show like Nailed It! and Floor Is Lava, and the kitchen will have crazy obstacles pop up to impede the chef's progress in crafting the perfect meal.

articles.title: Godzilla Minus Zero: Where Is the Rest of Godzilla’s Rogues' Gallery?
articles.summary: Where is the rest of Godzilla’s rogues' gallery? We take a look at Monster Island's most wanted.
articles.body:
Spoilers follow for Godzilla Minus Zero .

Godzilla Minus Zero is upon us, and going by the reviews , it looks like the venerable kaiju franchise has another winner on its hands. More than 70 years after his debut, Godzilla continues to be one of the most iconic characters in cinema history. But even though Minus Zero is another strong entry for the King of the Monsters, I couldn’t help but be a little disappointed that the movie continues a frustrating trend that’s plagued the last couple decades of Godzilla movies by only featuring a handful of his monster co-stars.

Specifically, King Ghidorah is the antagonist of Minus Zero, once again assuming his role as the Big G’s archenemy. Now, I love King Ghidorah, but the alien dragon takes up a lot of oxygen in Toho’s filmography, and there is a deep bench of Godzilla friends and foes who haven’t shown up in years. Let’s look into how the Godzilla franchise isn’t using its roster of monsters to their full potential.

Although most Western audiences probably haven’t seen many of them, Toho has produced more than 30 Godzilla films since the big guy’s debut back in 1954. Godzilla may have been the sole kaiju in his first film, but starting with the sequel, Godzilla Raids Again, the first of many monster co-stars was introduced. That would be Anguirus, an ankylosaur-like kaiju who was Godzilla’s earliest adversary. Luckily, the pair made up and Anguirus became Godzilla’s most steadfast ally across the Shōwa era, consisting of the first 15 films. Many kaiju have shared the screen with Godzilla over the years, but you wouldn’t know it if you’ve only been checking out new Godzilla movies released theatrically outside Japan.

Since Godzilla: Final Wars in 2004, the only Toho kaiju to have appeared in live-action are Mothra, Rodan, King Ghidorah, and Mechagodzilla. Kong doesn’t count in this context because he was created in America by Merian C. Cooper. Now those four may be among the most popular of Godzilla’s co-stars anyway, but there are many more that new films could revisit. However, since the MonsterVerse franchise apparently has to license each Toho monster individually, they often make up their own kaiju instead, like the MUTOs in the 2014 film or Skar King in Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire. Yet none of the new MonsterVerse kaiju have quite hit the same as the ones from the classic Toho films.

King Ghidorah’s overexposure is particularly frustrating because most uses of him are good, even if he keeps hogging the spotlight. He makes a great antithesis to the big guy in Godzilla: King of the Monsters, and his Minus Zero incarnation is terrifying and awe-inspiring in equal measure. In the new film, he’s an alien who’s crash-landed in postwar Japan and started claiming the land for his own purposes — an apt metaphor for the occupying American military that hovers over the story. So we wouldn’t want director Takashi Yamazaki to have foregone Ghidorah when his appearance in Minus Zero makes sense. King Ghidorah is basically the Joker to Godzilla’s Batman: It’s awesome when they square up, but sometimes you wish they’d go with a different bad guy. It’s not like there aren’t plenty to choose from.

Over the course of Toho’s 31 live-action Godzilla films, the big guy has encountered more than two dozen other kaiju. From fellow dinosaurs to alien invaders to mechanical guardians to mutated monstrosities, Toho’s monster roster is eclectic and extensive. The Shōwa, Heisei, and Millennium eras have all added new members to the group, but the latest batch of films in the Reiwa era have left many of them on the shelf. That’s not to say the Reiwa era films are bad, mind you — Shin Godzilla and the Minus films stand up with the best of the Big G’s filmography (we’ll politely refrain from talking about the animated Netflix trilogy). Yet there’s no denying that Toho’s Reiwa films and the concurrent MonsterVerse franchise aren’t taking full advantage of the cast of characters at their disposal.

Where is Gigan, the alien cyborg with scythe hands and a buzzsaw in his belly? Or Megalon, the bipedal rhinoceros beetle with drill hands who protects Seatopia, the Godzilla universe’s version of Atlantis? Or Biollante, the gargantuan plant queen that results from splicing Godzilla cells with a rose? They and many others have been eagerly awaiting a rematch with the King of the Monsters. Several other Heisei and Millennium era foes, such as Destoroyah, Orga, and Megaguirus have only made one film appearance each despite being well-liked by fans. In fact, the only live action Toho kaiju introduced after the Shōwa era to appear in more than one movie is Kiryu, a new version of Mechagodzilla constructed by the Japanese Self-Defense Forces using the bones of the 1954 Godzilla as a skeletal framework.

At least one Heisei monster seems to finally be escaping purgatory: SpaceGodzilla, who according to a Writer’s Guild of America registration , is set to appear in the upcoming Godzilla x Kong: Supernova. All well and good, but I hope the rest of Godzilla’s rogues' gallery is being considered for more appearances in the future, especially given how anxious fans are to see more of their favorite monsters, and the success the Godzilla franchise has enjoyed on multiple fronts over the past several years. Now is the perfect time to reintroduce the rest of Toho’s monsters to international audiences.

Some fans have argued that Toho exclusively focusing on their most popular monsters like Mothra, Rodan, and King Ghidorah is a sound business move because they’re the most recognizable Godzilla co-stars to audiences outside Japan. That may be true, but it doesn’t account for how Godzilla’s wider cast has been kept alive in the cultural imagination by expanded universe media. Comics, animated shows, and a legion of video games have often utilized monsters that the films have neglected, with the Pipeworks trilogy of fighting games — starting with Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee — introducing an entire generation of younger gamers to the Big G’s friends and foes. The enduring popularity of those games as a nostalgic touchstone resulted in DAMM recently being reborn with its Remastered edition.

The hunger from fans for other kaiju co-stars has even expressed itself in humorous ways. When the first teaser for Godzilla Minus Zero dropped in April, many fans joked that the blue gravity beams used by Ghidorah were actually going to belong to “Gravity Anguirus,” a hypothetical version of the character with new gravity manipulation powers. Gravity Anguirus may be a meme, but the way the joke spread across Godzilla fandom speaks to how much the people yearn to see Godzilla’s best friend back on the big screen. The poor guy must be feeling left out watching Godzilla and Kong go on adventures together. And as a personal note, what do I have to do to get my incompetent son Ebirah the giant lobster back in circulation?

At the end of the day, the Godzilla franchise is in a great spot. He’s got two successful movie series running simultaneously, Legacy of Monsters appears to be a hit on AppleTV+, and Destroy All Monsters Remastered has reignited Godzilla’s relevance in the gaming space. Toho’s stewardship of the series in the modern day is to be commended... but if there’s one place with room for improvement, it’s opening the door so the rest of their characters can share the spotlight. Godzilla, Mothra, Rodan, and King Ghidorah are all fantastic monsters; I’d just like to see the rest of their friends join them on the playground.

Carlos Morales writes novels, articles, and Mass Effect essays. You can follow his fixations on Twitter .

articles.title: Gundam Assemble: Hands-On With Mobile Suit Gundam’s Miniatures Tabletop Game
articles.summary: Get a closer look at the Gundam Assemble Starter Set.
articles.body:
The storied Mobile Suit Gundam series makes another venture into the tabletop world with Gundam Assemble, a new miniatures game experience. In fact, this new game was revealed alongside the Gundam Card Game as a visual companion, so fans got hit with a fun one-two punch of new game teases. Gundam Assemble is available for the first time this fall, with more expansion packs and sets already prepared to release into early next year. After a good chunk of time with the starter set, this game is shaping up to be a fun bite-size brawl compared to some of the other miniature games out there right now.

Arguably one of the biggest barriers of entry to miniature wargames is the building and painting aspect. If building is your biggest concern, have no fear with Gundam Assemble. Just like the gunpla that the series is known for, Gundam Assemble features pieces that you cut out and snap into place. Granted, the pieces are a lot smaller in comparison to regular gunpla, but it’s simplified, needing only a handful of parts to complete a mini Gundam unit. I suggest using proper cutting tools since these are miniatures and there’s less room for error. They look good though, showcasing a decent amount of detail for miniature versions of what fans are familiar with. Like other modern miniatures, assembly has been made a lot easier by simply snapping parts together as instructed, but it loses the customization that players may prefer with particular sets of miniature games. Instead, we see different variants or poses of Gundam units across the different releases. For instance, the RX-78-2 Gundam in the starter set features a beam saber attack, but the variant in the Paint Pack has the mech unit brandishing a beam rifle. Although not ideal for those that want a little bit of personal touch to their creations, it does make it easier for beginners (or even impatient players like myself) to jump right into painting and the gameplay soon after.

Gundam Assemble Starter Set 01 - Before and After Paint

Painting miniatures is not for the faint of heart, and Gundam Assemble isn’t any easier with all the tiny details, from the weapons to the mech head pieces. And if you’re a perfectionist, you’ll be spending more time painting than even playing the game. With that said, the mech units in the Gundam universe are fairly straightforward to paint with the mostly monochrome looks with embellishments littered about. Thankfully, there’s no skin or flesh color to deal with while painting Gundam units, which can be difficult to do properly. As long as you start off with a primer, you can save a bit of time, especially with units like the RX-78-2 or the Wing Gundam Zero. For me, I like to keep painting fairly simple because I just don’t have as much free time nowadays. And I care more about the gameplay than the arts and crafts of it all anyway. With that said, I do still want to make things look somewhat cool and clean compared to what I did as a 12-year-old painting Black Templar Space Marines because it was one of the easier chapters to paint. On the flip side, I’d prefer to skip painting altogether if possible, and that’s how I got into other miniature games like HeroClix and Star Wars X-Wing – where the minis were already painted. You can also just not paint the minis, but the extra effort does make for a better experience. The starter set even has a painting guide section in its instruction manual if you’re new to the hobby. Other than having some specific paints available like the Gundam Assemble Paint Pack, it’s also fine to use any water-based acrylic model paint and mix colors as need be. That’s how Char’s Zaku’s colors turned out when some friends and I had a dedicated paint day for some of these minis. Overall, painting is much easier now and it saves a ton of time if you do a bit of research before getting started.

As I mentioned, I care mostly about the gameplay when it comes to miniature games, and Gundam Assemble’s matches are surprisingly a smooth experience. I’m not in the miniatures tabletop scene constantly, but I dabble with some casual games every now and then like Marvel United. The hardest part is finding a buddy or group willing to learn the complex game mechanics and dedicating time and space to matches. It’s been kind of a sore spot for me and my friends lately, always talking about wanting to play Warhammer 40K Kill Team , but never fully committing because we still want to properly build and paint. With Gundam Assemble, it’s easier to get games going because you only really need six mech units versus a multitude of grunts to fill up a squad or army on either side. Although there are still a lot of tokens for various effects and objectives, the most important feature that makes turn-taking smooth is the Gundam Assemble timeline. It consists of ten rounds equaling one phase. On the timeline, players have their mech units’ tokens slotted into specific spots to help track each unit’s turn. For example, the Gundam Vidar has a timeline start number of one compared to RX-78-2’s timeline start number two. This means that Gundam Vidar places its token on round one of the timeline at setup, signifying that it takes its turn first before moving to round two, where RX-78-2’s token sits. As units make certain actions, their unit token moves down the timeline. So depending on what your mech unit does, they could be waiting a long time to act again. Seeing which mech is next in line does give an extra layer of strategy similar to turn-based tactics video games like XCOM or Star Wars Zero Company . It’s nice to have the timeline set to the side of the map and away from the battlefield where token placements can get out of hand.

In a common scenario, players play through two phases or 20 rounds, trying to collect as many victory points as possible through various means. Scoring victory points ranges from rescuing/destroying garrisons to defeating a mech unit or holding objective points at the end of each phase. Each mech unit’s turn consists of a few possible options: advance, primary action, command abilities, and tactics cards. Advance is simply movement, and units can move up to three hexes in any direction. Although, when it comes to moving up a level of terrain, it costs two hexes of movement. There’s no terrain penalty going down a level, and units with a Hover ability ignore terrain penalties all together. Primary actions move the unit token down the timeline and includes options like attack, dash, energize, and rescue. Attacks on the unit cards have specific timeline costs. So if the RX-78-2’s Beam Saber attack has a timeline of three, the Gundam’s token moves down the timeline three rounds after using this specific attack. The other three primary actions normally cost two timeline rounds. Dash is an option to move two hexes further. In Char’s Zaku’s case, dashes can also deal damage with his Char Kick ability. Next is energize, which gives a unit an energy token so they can use certain abilities later in the game. And the last primary action is rescue, which can be used to rescue friendly garrison tokens on the battlefield for victory points. Some units benefit from rescuing garrisons like the RX-78-2, which has a command ability that increases its strength by one for every garrison rescued. Speaking of command abilities, that’s another option available during a mech unit’s turn that’s printed on the unit card. These command abilities usually have an energy cost and/or specific requirement, so plan accordingly. And finally there are tactics cards, which can be used up to once a turn before being discarded. Players start off with three tactics cards but eventually draw more after a phase ends. These are one-time use, ranging from repairing a mech unit to using an entirely new attack or countering an enemy unit. It seems like a lot for one turn, but at most times, players are mainly just advancing and using a primary action as options on the battlefield start to dwindle.

Of course, we have to talk about the combat in a Gundam miniatures game. Since games are typically 3v3 mech units, the battlefield is not too cluttered with miniatures, so entering combat gameplay is fairly quick in the opening turns as they each get deployed onto the battlefield and disperse towards various objectives. When enemy units are in range, the player’s unit can choose one of two attacks printed on their card or possibly an attack Tactics card. Each attack has a strength number and that signals how many 10-sided dice to use to calculate hits, criticals, and damage. Four and greater is a hit which equals one damage, and nines or tens are critical hits that activate the attack’s crit effect – whether it’s additional damage or a negative effect that hinders a unit’s capabilities. Unlike other games, Gundam Assemble doesn’t have defensive rolls like saving throws, so its damage calculation can be fairly easy. Instead, defenses can be used in the form of Shield tokens that a unit can pick up by chance or applied via a command ability or tactics card. Shield tokens are passive bonuses that nullify one hit per token equipped, and become exhausted or deactivated until the start of that mech unit’s turn. For example, the Gundam Barbatos Lupus Rex’s Tail Blade attack attempts to deal six damage to Gundam Vidar, but the defending unit has two Shield tokens equipped. Instead of taking six damage, Gundam Vidar only takes four and the two Shield tokens are flipped over to signify being used. If another unit comes along to attack the Gundam Vidar before it reactivates its Shield tokens, the tokens will not defend two hits of damage. This, alongside some abilities or tactics cards that can nullify or lessen damage, keep combat rolls fairly quick and seamless. There’s no need to calculate a multitude of faction bonuses or if a unit is concealed or aiming like in other miniature wargames so far. The only other consideration when attacking is accuracy, which can be altered by elevation or special terrain like water. When a mech unit is eventually defeated, the winning player gains victory points as noted on the enemy unit’s card. Then the enemy unit’s token on the timeline is moved two spaces ahead when it can redeploy again after ‘repairs’ have been made. Any upgrades or energy accumulated stay with the defeated mech unit until it deploys again.

One other thing worth mentioning when it comes to any miniatures games is the price. After all, these detailed minis are a step above acrylic or cardboard standees or tokens, and it can get overwhelming when deciding which units to collect. The Gundam Assemble Starter Set 01 will run you about $35, which isn’t that much more than a HG gunpla kit, depending on the model. Considering a starter set of Warhammer 40K Kill Team can run you about $118 or a Star Wars Legion starter at about $99, Gundam Assemble is much easier on the wallet. I know my mom would’ve appreciated that when I first got into Warhammer 40K back in the day. With that said, there is a Deluxe Starter Set for Gundam Assemble at about $100, which contains double the minis of a regular starter. And if you’re feeling the itch, there are expansion packs featuring fan favorites that can run you $40.

Gundam Assemble’s gameplay is a nice blend of objective-based scoring while also having the option to just all-out attack enemy units for their VP rewards. It’s the balance of managing both strategies to your units’ best abilities that determines who is the better tactician. Between the easy builds that gunpla and miniature fans are familiar with to the fairly quick instances of combat and timeline management, the barrier to entry is slightly more beginner-friendly than other starter sets in the miniature wargame landscape. Not to mention, the price isn’t too bad for Gundam fans interested in a new tabletop experience, or those looking to venture into miniature games for the first time. For more Gundam, check out our hands-on impressions of the Gundam Card Game or our interview with the Director of Gundam RG XARX-Zero, Kenji Kamiyama .

Mike Mamon is a Syndication & Digital Specialist at IGN, devil fruit user, and world-renown JoJo poser. Let's chat anime or TCGs on Bluesky @xpmnms.bsky.social

articles.title: Secrets of the Baishan Sect - Phantom Blade Zero Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Secrets of the Baishan Sect is a missable Tale that can be easily skipped over in Crimson Forest. To begin this quest, you need to defeat Hua Qianxiao, the
articles.body:
Secrets of the Baishan Sect is a missable Tale that can be easily skipped over in Crimson Forest. To begin this quest, you need to defeat Hua Qianxiao, the Sword Fanatic and Jing Ye, The Outlaw . These are both mandatory bosses.

Just after Jing Ye, you will come across a bridge with two women standing on it. Speak to the one in blue to begin the quest. She will mention that Sister Meng has lost all reason, requesting you to find her.

Here are the steps to complete the quest:

Progress through the Crimson Forest until you reach the Cliffside Lodge bell. This is just before the cutscene where Soul is chased by the Crusher and the Saw.

Head behind the lodge and climb the ladder to the top of the building. These rooms are poison-filled so you will need to heal every few seconds to survive exploring the top of the lodge.

Head to the ledge on the upper floor to find the Crimson Forest Cellar Crank, which can be used on the floor beneath you.

Find The Crimson Forest Secret Chamber Crank

Open the lock on the base floor of the cliffside lodge and enter the room below that opens up. The sister can be found behind a locked gate. Thankfully, the crank to open it is in these rooms under the lodge.

Before you grab it, climb up the wall further into the room and hop onto the cliff with the red item. This has the Thieves' Camp Dungeon Key, which is needed for the Healer's Mercy quest.

Jump back down and climb the wall again to find another walkway you can jump down to, underneath the path you were just on. Here, you can find the Crimson Forest Secret Chamber Crank and a Blackstone Shard in the chest.

With the Crank, jump back down to the base floor of this underground cellar. Head towards where you picked up the Thieves' Camp Dungeon Key and take a left.

Here you can find the chamber with the disciple. Open it with the crank and talk to her.

articles.title: A Healer's Mercy - Lost Thief Locations - Phantom Blade Zero Guide - IGN
articles.summary: A Healer's Mercy is a missable side quest in Phantom Blade Zero. Classed as a Tale, this side quest can be started once you meet with Yu'er at the
articles.body:
A Healer's Mercy is a missable side quest in Phantom Blade Zero . Classed as a Tale, this side quest can be started once you meet with Yu'er at the Thieves' Camp in the Crimson Forest.

Talk to her and choose the option "The Wounded in the Woods". She and the thief next to her will mention that some of the other thieves in the forest are still missing and you need to hunt them down. You will also get a pill, which is a story item needed to heal the thieves.

There are four Lost Thief locations scattered across the Crimson Forest.

Travel back to the Outlaw Trap bell, just before you beat Jing Ye, The Outlaw . Head into the cave to the right of the bell to find the first thief.

Zhou the "Lean Monkey" can be found in the tunnel beneath the Outlaw Bell.

To open this, you will need to get the Crimson Forest Tunnel Crank. This can be found in the cave where you found Li the "Flying Rat".

Use the crank on the lock by the Outlaw Trap bell and jump down.

Follow the path over the walkway (where the enemies are) and take the path to the left. Here you can find Zhou.

Next, progress all the way to the Cliffside Lodge. Follow our quest guide or the first steps of the Secrets of the Baishan Sect Tale to reach Zhen.

Make sure you grab the Thieves' Camp Dungeon Key too, which is detailed on that page. After you free the Baishan Disciple, head out of the cellar and open the door.

Just outside you can find Zhen. Heal him by talking to him.
